rulings.Rulings: Continued to 10/28/26. (No earlier availability.) (1) An amended petition was just filed on 8/17/26. Trusts require 30 days' notice. (2) Notice is defective if mailed before the filing of the pleading requiring notice. [LRSF 14.14 A.] "Filing" means when the pleading requiring notice appears on the Court's register of actions and becomes publicly viewable. (3) An "amended pleading" means a pleading that completely restates and supersedes the pleading it amends for all purposes. [CRC 7.3(3).] The amended petition appears to refer to things that an amended petition should not, such as issues related to the original petition. (The amended petition has not yet been fully reviewed, as no courtesy copy was provided, as required by LRSF 2.7 B. and 14.7 B.) (4) The fiduciary or the attorney for the fiduciary must make the ex parte application immediately upon becoming aware of the need to increase bond. [CRC 7.204.] Deadline to provide the assigned examiner a revised proposed order and courtesy copies of the amended petition and proof of service of notice of the amended petition mailed at least 30 days before 10/28/26 is 10/14/26. Courtesy copies are file stamped, single-sided, hard copies. [LRSF 14.7 B. and C.] Examiner continuances are final and not subject to contest under LRSF 14.10 B. rulings.Case Title: IN THE MATTER OF THE ROBERT P. CLARKE REVOCABLE TRUST DATED 3/28/23
rulings.Calendar Matter: REPORT OF SALE AND PETITION TO CONFIRM SALE OF REAL PROPERTY (627 22nd Ave, San Francisco, Ca 94121)
rulings.Rulings: Hearing. Appearance required. The judicial officer is to review and determine: 1) The reported sale was made (offer was accepted and purchase contract signed) on 08/04/2026, BEFORE notice of sale was first published on 08/27/2026. The published notice did not state the day on or after which the sale is to be made (see Probate Code section 10300(b)(1)) or the place at which bids or offers will be received (see section 10304(a)(2)). As such, the reported sale failed to comply with section 10306(a)("A private sale of real property may not be made before the day stated in the notice of sale as the day on or after which the sale will be made"); see also LRSF 14.31B ("No offer can be accepted until the date on or after the time for making bids expires."). Section 10312 provides that: "If notice of the sale was required, before an order is made confirming the sale it shall be proved to the satisfaction of the court that notice of the sale was given as required by this article, and the order of confirmation shall show that the proof was made." As the trust remains under the Court's supervision, the trustee is subject to the same terms and conditions as a conservator of the estate, unless waived upon a showing of good cause. See LRSF 14.47(B)(5). 2) Paragraph 12b of the proposed order purports to approve a 5% commission to be equally divided between the seller's broker and buyers' broker, but the Court's May 27, 2026 order that authorized this sale specified a broker commission of no more than 3%. While a 2.5% commission payable to the seller's broker can be approved on the order confirming this sale, no determination can be made as to whether any commission should be paid out of the sale proceeds to the buyers' broker, although the order not providing for approval of the buyers' broker's commission is without prejudice to the buyers' contractual right to enforce the seller's obligation to credit the buyers 2.5% of the price under paragraph 7 of the purchase agreement to be used to compensate the buyers' broker.
